subject: Follow-up: prompt bucket & evaluation readiness — ClauseIQ
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clauseiq.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@legalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: prompt bucket & evaluation readiness — ClauseIQ

Hi Samir / Marta —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- What we heard: ClauseIQ wants a QA assistant that can (a) summarize clauses, (b) extract obligations and dates, and (c) highlight risky language with examples. You flagged long tail/rare clause templates and customer-facing PII concerns.
- Immediate ask from your side: a representative set of real user queries (no full documents) and any internal examples of edge-case clauses you worry about. You mentioned you can share a small CSV of queries + labels.
- Redwood's plan: we’ll run a 2-week eval with 3 model variants, produce token-cost/latency tradeoffs, and surface sample failure modes. We’ll also provide a redaction checklist template and guidance for safe prompt collection.

For the eval we recommend starting with: redwood-7b-q4 (fast + low cost), redwood-13b-fp16 (balanced), and redwood-34b-quant (higher quality for extraction-heavy tasks). Ben will attach the short benchmark matrix and Laura will own the evaluation rubric.

Action items:
1) Samir / Marta: please share a first-pass prompt bucket (100–300 representative queries) and mark any items that contain PII or are regulated. If you have a CSV, great — otherwise paste examples inline.
2) Redwood: we’ll send a redaction checklist and a secure upload link.
3) Joint: schedule a 30-min sync next Thursday to review initial eval results.

Attachments referenced: redaction_checklist_template.docx (we’ll populate once you confirm constraints).

If any of this is off, flag it — otherwise we’ll get the secure upload link out today.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

---

From: Samir Patel <samir@clauseiq.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta@legalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 11:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt bucket & evaluation readiness — ClauseIQ

Thanks Jasmine — that aligns with our notes. Quick answers and a few inline examples to seed the bucket: 

- PII/regulatory constraints: we cannot share full contracts or any unredacted customer names / SSNs / tax IDs. Clause identifiers and clause text are fine when redacted for party names.

Sample queries (paste):
1) "Extract all termination notice periods and associated notice email address"
2) "List obligations that require vendor consent before data transfer"
3) "Summarize the indemnity clause in plain English (max 3 bullets)"
4) "Flag any monetary caps and currency referenced"

We’ll upload a CSV with 180 rows later today. Two asks for Redwood: 1) a short PII redaction checklist (we need a single doc we can run past legal); 2) confirmation that the secure upload will be S3 (pre-signed) or direct Drive link.

On timelines: 2-week eval sounds good. Can the first pass include a focused extraction accuracy metric (precision/recall) for obligations? That’s critical for us.

—Samir
Head of Product, ClauseIQ

Samir —

We can definitely include precision/recall for obligation extraction as a primary metric. Quick notes on model choices:
- redwood-7b-q4: excellent latency for sampling/interactive workflows; expect lower recall on very long multi-clause paragraphs.
- redwood-13b-fp16: good balance — strong on extraction with moderate cost.
- redwood-34b-quant: best absolute extraction performance in our bench, but higher cost and longer tail latency.

I’ve uploaded a short benchmark summary here: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/202811/redwood-model-summary (public within our org). Laura, I’ll sync with you on the rubric and templated eval spreadsheet.

—Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — we attached the CSV in this reply (clauseiq_query_samples.csv). The file contains: query_text, example_contract_template, expected_extraction_labels. We redacted party names and replaced emails with <REDACTED_EMAIL>.

One additional constraint: some templates contain nested obligations (obligation A modifies obligation B). We’ll flag those rows with "nested":true.

Also attaching our internal note on compliance constraints (redaction_requirements.pdf). Please confirm you can consume CSV columns as-is or if you prefer a different schema.

Best,

Samir / Marta —

Received the CSV and compliance note, thanks — I pulled both into the secure intake. Next steps from Redwood side: 

1) Redaction: we’ll apply your redaction rules to the dataset and send back a sanitized sample within 24 hours. We’ll use the redaction_checklist_template.docx to capture decisions and will ask for sign-off from your legal team.
2) Eval plan: Ben/Laura will run the 2-week run across the three model families. Deliverables at the end of week 2: a short deck (SLOs, precision/recall tables, latency/cost matrix), 10 representative failure examples (with suggested prompt fixes), and a recommendation for production model + quantization profile.
3) Secure upload: we created a pre-signed S3 bucket (expiring links) and emailed the intake instructions to Samir separately. If you prefer Drive instead tell us and we’ll switch.

Quick clarifications:
- We will measure obligation extraction precision/recall at the clause-level (not token-level) and include a separate metric for nested-obligations.
- For prompts that include PII we’ll request redacted variants; do not send raw PII via email.

Proposed sync: Fri Dec 8, 09:00 PT — 30 minutes to review first-pass results. I’ll send the invite after you confirm.

Thanks again — we’ll post interim results to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_clauseiq_prompt_playbook and the internal benchmark page above.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
